blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. This section was written from Tsawwassen First Nation's own Land Use Plan Update site (landuseplan.tsawwassenfirstnation.com) and replaces text that was repeated on the other Tsawwassen guides. Pages from the City of Delta, BC Ferries, TransLink, the school district and Statistics Canada could not be opened during research, so nothing from them is used here. See the open items list.
Treaty land north of Highway 17

Part of what buyers search as Tsawwassen North is Tsawwassen Lands, the lands governed by Tsawwassen First Nation (TFN). Before you compare homes, it helps to know how that came about, because it affects who sets the rules for your street.

TFN's land use plan site says the Tsawwassen people have lived around the Salish Sea and the lower Fraser River since time immemorial. Their way of life centred on fishing, hunting and trade, with salmon, sturgeon, crab and eulachon at the heart of food and culture. The site also records dispossession and the imposition of the Indian Act, and says the community kept its identity through it.

The Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement took effect in 2009. TFN describes it as the first urban modern treaty in British Columbia, and it recognized TFN's self-government and jurisdiction over its lands. A Land Use Plan was adopted the same year. Since then TFN has signed a 99-year lease for Tsawwassen Mills, one of Canada's largest shopping centres, and has finished a $27 million sewage treatment plant. It bought 80 hectares at Brunswick Point in 2019, and 70 of those hectares were brought into Tsawwassen Lands in 2024.

TFN's site also tells the story of Princess Tsawwassa, Chief Stetson's daughter. In a leadership challenge she outdid her brothers by bringing back a wider range of foods, including wild onions. A house post at the TFN Sports Field honours her.
From about 200 leasehold homes to about 2,000

The growth is recent, and TFN publishes the figures. The table below uses its numbers only. The 2,000 leasehold unit figure is written as "2000 units" on the plan site, so ask TFN to confirm it if you are quoting it.

blocks.text: What that means for you: this is a young neighbourhood that is still being finished. Roads, parks and services are still being added, so ask what is planned beside any address you are considering, not just what stands there today.
How the land is divided
The plan sorts Tsawwassen Lands into five broad areas. Two matter most to home buyers: the leasehold Neighbourhood, and the Mixed Use Area around the two shopping centres.

blocks.text: Herons, marsh and green space

The plan treats the Tidal Marsh and the Bluff as ecological management zones that protect wildlife habitat, medicinal plants and archaeological sites. The Bluff holds a heron rookery of about 400 nests, with more than 800 birds there year-round. The plan also describes Great Blue Heron Way, a cultural and ecological trail connecting TFN to neighbouring Nations.

For parks, the plan says TFN upgraded an existing community park and is adding new ones through development. It wants them safe, welcoming, accessible and connected to neighbourhoods and schools. The plan site also mentions a community farm pilot, with goats used to control invasive plants. If a home backs onto the marsh or the bluff, ask TFN what limits apply there before you rely on the view.
Roads and getting around

Highway 17 and Deltaport Way cut through Tsawwassen Lands. The plan names five key internal roads: 52nd Street, Salish Sea Drive, Salish Sea Way, Tsawwassen Drive and 41B Street. It lists the 41B Street overpass among the places where TFN will keep watching traffic, and it says developers must dedicate land for roads and trails.

The plan puts weight on walking and cycling, and wants the Mixed Use Area to be walkable and transit-friendly, with bike-friendly streets and better transit. TFN says TransLink provides its public transit and that it works with TransLink on service within Tsawwassen Lands and the links out of them. Water comes from Metro Vancouver. Before you buy, try the trip to work at the hours you would really travel, and ask TransLink for the current timetable for the stops near your address.
What the plan means for buyers and owners

Because the Neighbourhood is leasehold, the lease is as important as the building. In general, you hold a long-term lease on the land instead of owning it outright. The lease and strata documents set out the term, what happens when it ends, what you can do with the unit, and what you can sell. Have a lawyer read them before you remove subjects, and ask your lender early whether they will finance the specific lease.

Change is also coming. TFN says it will prepare a Mixed Use Area Plan, an Industrial and Employment Lands Secondary Plan and a Brunswick Point Lands Growth Plan. It lists the 13-Acre Parcel and the Industrial Waterfront Parcel as study areas where housing is one of the uses under consideration. None of those decisions are made, so treat them as questions to ask rather than promises. The update's engagement ran from September 2023 to June 2025, with 24 sessions and more than 350 Member participations.

Finally, the plan covers Tsawwassen Lands only. An MLS sub-area name does not tell you whose land an address is on. Send me the address and I will check which jurisdiction applies before you write an offer.
Condo buildings in Tsawwassen North
5099 Springs Boulevard — the earliest condo building verified
MLS listings for units record year built 2011, geothermal heating, elevator, underground parking, 4 storeys for the units read, in the Tsawwassen Springs subdivision / Tsawwassen North sub-area.
5055 Springs Boulevard

The developer's own site publishes condo floor plans for 5055 Springs Boulevard (including a 2-bedroom + den penthouse plan, "Condo T"). A listing for a unit records year built 2014, concrete construction, geothermal heating/cooling and EV parking.
5011 Springs Boulevard — the Phase 3 condo

The developer's construction updates describe drilling 88 geo-exchange boreholes (240 feet deep) for the Phase 3 condo at 5011 Springs Boulevard. MLS listings for units record year built 2018, concrete construction, geothermal heating and air conditioning, underground parking, and strata-fee inclusions recorded for a unit as caretaker, garbage, heat, hot water and sewer.
Streets, schools and getting around Tsawwassen North

items.t: The defining boundary on this side is a jurisdictional one: the north side sits beside Tsawwassen First Nation Lands. Tsawwassen First Nation is self-governing, with jurisdiction over land management on Tsawwassen Lands — over 724 hectares transferred under the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement — so City of Delta zoning does not apply on Tsawwassen Lands.
Main roads: Highway 17 (to the BC Ferries Tsawwassen terminal and to Highway 17A), 52 Street, 56 Street and Canoe Pass Way; Highway 17A leads to Highway 99 and the George Massey Tunnel.

Transit: route 609 runs from South Delta Exchange via 56 Street, 12 Avenue, 52 Street and Canoe Pass Way, through Tsawwassen First Nation, to Ladner Exchange; route 601 serves 56 Street and South Delta Exchange toward Bridgeport Station.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: in one development — Tsawwassen Springs, on Springs Boulevard at 52 Street, around the golf course. The rest of the City-of-Delta side is single detached houses under the RS and RD zones on the streets south of Highway 17, with farm and ALR land between Tsawwassen and Ladner.

Services are south or on the corridor: South Delta Recreation Centre, 1720 56 St at South Delta Exchange; Tsawwassen Library, 1321A 56 St; Thrifty Foods on the Town Centre Mall site (1219 56 Street, 5499 12 Avenue, 1236 55 Street); and Fraser Health's South Delta After-Hours Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 1826 – 4949 Canoe Pass Way, on the Canoe Pass Way corridor.
Every address must be checked in the locator.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Tsawwassen North

items.t: Jurisdiction first: City of Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 and OCP Bylaw No. 8400 apply only to the City side. On Tsawwassen Lands, Tsawwassen First Nation jurisdiction and land law apply instead — tenure, servicing and resale handling differ, and a buyer must establish which side of the boundary a property sits on before anything else.
Age bylaws: only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1, 123.2); lower ages have been invalid since Nov 24, 2022, and the rule binds residents, not owners.

Delta zoning (City side): Bylaw No. 7600 residential ladder includes RS4 at a 610 m² subdivision minimum, RS5 at 550 m² or 460 m², RS6 at 390 m², RS7 at 335 m², RD1 at 836 m² and RD4 at 504 m², confirmed parcel by parcel on the City zoning maps.
Presales and assignments (REDMA): a presale buyer has a 7-day statutory rescission period from the later of signing or disclosure-statement acknowledgement, with deposits held in trust.

blocks.text: Good to know about Tsawwassen North

items.t: The Springs was built in phases over most of a decade, and the phases are different buildings: listings date 5099 Springs Boulevard to 2011, 5055 to 2014 and 5011 (the developer's "Phase 3 Condo") to 2018 — age, warranty history and depreciation position differ by address, not by brand.

The geothermal system is literally under the buildings: the developer's Phase 3 construction update describes 88 boreholes drilled 240 feet deep for the geo-exchange system at 5011 Springs Boulevard — the heating/cooling plant a buyer's depreciation report has to account for.

More product is already in the City's pipeline on the same street: a townhouse project at 4800 Springs Boulevard (with a portion of 5133 Springs Boulevard) appears on the City of Delta housing projects map — the next phase of the Springs Boulevard corridor to check before paying a scarcity premium.

The bus goes through a First Nation to get to Ladner: route 609's path via Canoe Pass Way passes through Tsawwassen First Nation — a reminder that the "north side" is a shared landscape of City land, TFN Lands and farm land, each with its own rules.

The urgent-care address buyers drive past is on Canoe Pass Way: Fraser Health's South Delta After-Hours Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 1826 – 4949 Canoe Pass Way, on this side of Tsawwassen; the hospital is Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Blvd, in Ladner.

SSMUH is the quiet change on the older streets south of Highway 17: since Bylaws 8394 and 8395 (Jun 24, 2024), detached and duplex lots on the City side can carry up to four units — the infill pressure to watch around the established detached streets, while the farm belt to Ladner stays ALR.

items.t: The rest of the City side is single detached houses under the RS and RD zones south of Highway 17, with farm and ALR land between Tsawwassen and Ladner.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Tsawwassen North

items.t: Jurisdiction first — the rule that decides everything in this sub-area: City of Delta zoning and the BC Strata Property Act's freehold-strata regime govern the City side. On Tsawwassen Lands, Tsawwassen First Nation jurisdiction and land law apply instead, and the townhouse product there is held under 99-year prepaid leases (Boardwalk) or leasehold prepaid-strata plans (Seaside). A buyer must establish which side of the boundary a property sits on, and which tenure document they are actually buying, before pricing anything.

City-side strata (when the 4800 Springs project, or any City-side strata townhouse, completes): the Form B regime: Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Depreciation reports (City-side strata): since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote; a strata corporation established on or after July 1, 2024 and before July 1, 2027 must obtain its first report within two years of its first AGM — the timeline that will apply to any brand-new north-side strata. CRF minimum: since Nov 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Rental-restriction bylaws are void (City-side strata): Nov 24, 2022 — no BC strata residential rental-restriction bylaw is valid; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw. Whether and how that provincial rule interacts with a specific TFN leasehold project's own documents is a per-project legal question.

Age bylaws (City-side strata): only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1, 123.2), with Regulation 7.01 exemptions expanded May 1, 2023. No 55+ bylaw is verified for any north-side complex, City-side or TFN-side.

Delta plan (City side): OCP Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), consolidated; farm land is designated "Agriculture (A)," and Agricultural Land Commission rules apply to land in the ALR, including one-residence-per-parcel limits relevant to large lots at the farm edge.

SSMUH (City side): Bylaws No. 8394 and 8395, adopted June 24, 2024 — four units on all residential properties in Delta; six within 400 m of frequent transit along Scott Road (North Delta). This applies to City-side detached/duplex lots, not to TFN Lands.

ALR stratification bar (farm edges): an ALR residence cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). Farm-status thresholds run in three tiers — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of land value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error.

Flood (City side): farm and ALR land lies between Tsawwassen and Ladner, and Delta is the diking authority operating over 63 km of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 km of drainage infrastructure.

Presales (REDMA) — live on the TFN side: Boardwalk phases are sold as presales; a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust — and for TFN product the disclosure package is also where the lease structure is spelled out. Read both together.

Delta property taxes (City side): 2026 due date July 2, 2026; 5% penalty after, further 5% after September 2, 2026. Tax administration on a specific Tsawwassen Lands property is a separate question to confirm for that property.

blocks.text: Good to know about Tsawwassen North

items.t: The treaty-land boundary is the single biggest townhouse fact on the north side. Homes a few blocks apart sit under entirely different governments and tenures: City of Delta freehold/strata law on one side, Tsawwassen First Nation jurisdiction (724+ hectares under the Final Agreement) and 99-year leasehold product on the other. Establish which side a property is on before pricing tenure, servicing or resale.

More City-side product is in the pipeline on the same street: the townhouse project at 4800 Springs Boulevard (with a portion of 5133 Springs Boulevard) on the City housing projects map is the next phase of the Springs Boulevard corridor to check before paying a scarcity premium for TFN leasehold product on the ground that "nothing else is coming."

SSMUH is the quiet change on the older City-side streets south of Highway 17: since Bylaws 8394 and 8395 (Jun 24, 2024), detached and duplex lots on the City side can carry up to four units — infill pressure to watch around the established detached streets, while the farm belt to Ladner stays ALR and TFN Lands follow TFN law, not the City bylaw.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Tsawwassen North
City side

items.t: Fee-simple detached lots south of Highway 17: Typical City-side types are single detached houses under the RS and RD zones on the residential streets south of Highway 17, plus newer strata housing around Springs Boulevard. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Lot character: urban residential subdivision minimums run from RS7 at 335 m² to RD1 at 836 m² (RS4 610 m², RS5 550/460 m², RS6 390 m², RD4 504 m² in the ladder); lots fronting the farm belt and Highway 17 corridor can be larger rural parcels, confirmed parcel by parcel. These are minimums, not a claim about any individual parcel.
Bare-land strata, City side: none verified

ALR / farm belt: farm and ALR land lies between Tsawwassen and Ladner on the north side's edge — the ground that separates the two communities. No area-wide ALR split is published and none is stated; a specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address, and ALC rules govern where it applies.

Serviced vs unserviced ground: no parcel-level servicing statement for North lots is documented. Confirm with the governing jurisdiction for the parcel; for an unserviced City-side parcel, GWELLS plus Fraser Health's onsite-sewerage position.

blocks.text: Development site

items.t: No completed complex, no strata plan, no unit count and no tenure (strata vs fee-simple) is published in the City snapshot read. It is a development site in process, not lots for sale and not built stock.

Tsawwassen Springs — Springs Boulevard at 52 Street (Shato Holdings / Talisman Homes): Neither the condos nor the detached houses are land inventory, and the Springs name alone never tells a buyer they are looking at a lot or a townhouse.

blocks.text: TFN leasehold land

items.t: Boardwalk, including Boardwalk6 — Tsawwassen First Nation, by Aquilini / TFSI Development. LEASEHOLD: Boardwalk6 is a collection of 22 parkside townhomes; the presale source states the ownership form expressly: "Leasehold via a 99-year prepaid lease," with the First Nation landowners leasing to the developer, which subleases to homeowners for 99 years; the developer's own site repeats that homes at Boardwalk are purchased with a 99-year leasehold. Excluded from fee-simple land stock because the land is Tsawwassen Lands held under that lease structure, under TFN law — a buyer acquires a leasehold interest, not fee-simple title to the land.

Tsawwassen Landing — 4738 Hemlock Way, by Onni Group. TFN / LEASEHOLD ground: A townhouse and single-family home community on Tsawwassen Lands (project sources place it on Tsawwassen Drive North / Hemlock Way, completed 2022 in the project listing read). It sits under Tsawwassen First Nation jurisdiction, not City of Delta zoning — excluded from City-side fee-simple stock on the same leasehold/jurisdiction ground; a project-specific lease document for a given unit must be read before any finer tenure statement is made about that unit.

Seaside (Seaside by Mosaic) — Orca Way. LEASEHOLD PREPAID-strata: MLS full reports record townhouse units in Seaside in the Tsawwassen North board area, built 2019–2022, with Title to Land: Leasehold prepaid-Strata, strata plans EPS4960 and EPS5770 in the reports read. Excluded from the fee-simple count on the same ground.

Tsawwassen Shores generally: the wider TFN residential development (over 1,500 homes on leasehold land in a neighbourhood source's description, including townhouses) is leasehold product on treaty land — the general statement behind the three named exclusions above. A TFN-lands parcel or leasehold interest surfacing in a land feed is not a freehold lot.
Boardwalk phases are sold as presale HOMES (REDMA), not as vacant lots; no TFN phase is documented as selling vacant serviced lots to individual builders.

blocks.text: Excluded

items.t: Tsawwassen RV Resort — 4761 Nulelum Way (Tsawwassen Lands): A manufactured-home / land-lease community described by its park source as all-ages.

items.t: The defining boundary is jurisdictional: the north side sits beside Tsawwassen First Nation Lands. Tsawwassen First Nation is a self-governing First Nation with jurisdiction over land management on Tsawwassen Lands — over 724 hectares transferred under the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement — so TFN land follows TFN law, not City of Delta bylaws, and City zoning does not apply on Tsawwassen Lands.
Nearby areas: Tsawwassen Central to the south, Ladner across the farm belt to the north, Tsawwassen First Nation Lands to the west and north.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Tsawwassen North

items.t: Jurisdiction first — the rule that decides everything here: City of Delta zoning and BC fee-simple/freehold-strata law govern the City side. On Tsawwassen Lands, TFN land follows TFN law, not City of Delta bylaws — Tsawwassen First Nation is self-governing with jurisdiction over land management on Tsawwassen Lands (724+ hectares under the Final Agreement), and the residential product there is held under 99-year prepaid leases (Boardwalk) or leasehold prepaid-strata plans (Seaside). Establish which side of the boundary a parcel sits on, and which tenure document is actually being bought, before pricing anything.
OCP (City side): Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), consolidated. Farm land is designated "Agriculture (A)". The OCP does not govern Tsawwassen Lands.

Delta zoning number: contested — flagged, never asserted (City side): (sheets cite No. 7600, 2017; an internal title reads "8400, 2025"). Residential ladder: RS4 610 m², RS5 550/460 m², RS6 390 m², RS7 335 m², RD1 836 m², RD4 504 m² subdivision minimums, parcel by parcel.

SSMUH (City side only): Bylaws 8394 and 8395, adopted June 24, 2024: — four units on all residential properties in Delta; six within 400 m of frequent transit along Scott Road (North Delta). Added units are not subdivision, and SSMUH does not apply on Tsawwassen Lands. Subdivision/servicing (City side): Development and Subdivision Standards Bylaw No. 8288, 2024 (repealing No. 7162, 2015), under LGA s. 506.

ALR rules (farm-belt parcels): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, as the ALC states it, including one-residence-per-parcel limits relevant to large lots at the farm edge. ALC caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class — three-tier, in full: $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" statement is an error.

Strata block (City-side strata, and any future 4800 Springs strata): Form B (SPA s. 59) — fees, amounts owed, levies still payable, CRF balance, insurance summary, with rules/budget/depreciation report attached; within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page. Depreciation reports every 5 years for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (a strata established on/after July 1, 2024 and before July 1, 2027 must obtain its first report within two years of its first AGM). CRF minimum 10% since November 1, 2023. Rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). Whether and how each provincial strata rule interacts with a specific TFN leasehold project's own documents is a per-project legal question.

GST on vacant land at CRA GI-003 level only: most individual personal-use sales exempt; business-use, in-the-course-of-business and more-than-two-part subdivision sales can be taxable; developer/newly-subdivided lots generally TAXABLE. FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122; 100% to $1M, max $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031) applies to new HOUSING, not bare land itself. New Housing Rebate 36% / max $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000. HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000 per year; CMHC 0.6%–4.5%. How each applies to a specific TFN leasehold purchase is a lawyer/notary question for that tenure — do not assume the freehold answer.

Speculation/vacancy taxes — the boundary in tax form: the Province's SVT taxable-areas list includes the City of Delta and states expressly that reserve lands, treaty lands and lands of self-governing Indigenous Nations are not part of the taxable areas — so Tsawwassen Lands are excluded from SVT taxable areas on the Province's own list, while City-side Delta parcels are in a listed area. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax (3%) is Vancouver only.

Delta property taxes (City side): due July 2, 2026; 5% penalty after, further 5% after September 2, 2026. Tax administration on a specific Tsawwassen Lands property is a separate question to confirm for that property. Foreclosure: Delta has no Supreme Court registry.

items.t: The treaty-land boundary is the single biggest land fact on the north side. Parcels a few blocks apart sit under entirely different governments and tenures: City fee-simple/strata law on one side, TFN jurisdiction and 99-year leasehold product on the other — and the tax map follows the same line (Delta listed for SVT; treaty/self-governing lands excluded). Establish which side a parcel is on before pricing tenure, servicing or resale.

The bus goes through a First Nation to get to Ladner: route 609 via Canoe Pass Way passes through Tsawwassen First Nation — a daily reminder that the "north side" is a shared landscape of City land, TFN Lands and farm land, each with its own rules.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Tsawwassen North
What acreage trades in Tsawwassen North: honestly, there is no verified acreage market on either side of this ground's jurisdictional boundary.
The ground in Tsawwassen North

items.t: City-side parcels are house lots, not acreages: The urban residential subdivision minimums in the applicable ladder run from RS7 at 335 m² to RD1 at 836 m² (RS4 610 m², RS5 550 m² or 460 m², RS6 390 m², RD4 504 m²) — these are lot minimums for houses, confirmed parcel by parcel on the City zoning maps, not acreage sizes.
Any specific large lot is judged on its own title, zone and ALR status.

Tsawwassen Springs: Tsawwassen Springs, on Springs Boulevard at 52 Street, is a Shato Holdings / Talisman Homes project (developer source), with condo buildings at 5011 Springs Boulevard and 5055 Springs Boulevard (developer source).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Tsawwassen North

items.t: Municipality: City of Delta, BC. Tsawwassen North is the north side of the Tsawwassen community, along Highway 17 and 52 Street toward Ladner, planned under the Delta Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) — the current OCP consolidated the former area plans into a single Land Use Plan.

Treaty-land boundary: the north side sits beside Tsawwassen First Nation Lands. Tsawwassen First Nation is a self-governing First Nation with jurisdiction over land management on Tsawwassen Lands — over 724 hectares transferred under the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement — so City of Delta zoning does not apply on Tsawwassen Lands.

Community anchors: South Delta Recreation Centre, 1720 56 St, at South Delta Exchange; Tsawwassen Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), 1321A 56 St; Thrifty Foods sits on the Tsawwassen Town Centre Mall site (City-listed site addresses 1219 56 Street, 5499 12 Avenue and 1236 55 Street).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Tsawwassen North

items.t: If a strata purchase is made on the City side (Springs Boulevard product): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw. None of this applies to a fee-simple parcel purchase itself.

faq.a: Parts of it are Tsawwassen Lands, which TFN governs under its 2009 treaty. TFN's plan names the leasehold Neighbourhood and the Tsawwassen Mills and Tsawwassen Commons parcels as part of those lands. The plan does not publish the MLS sub-area boundary, so confirm any address with TFN and the City of Delta.
faq.q: Is Tsawwassen North on City of Delta land or Tsawwassen First Nation land?

faq.a: TFN's plan describes the Neighbourhood as leasehold residential. In general, you hold a long-term lease on the land rather than owning it outright. The lease sets out the term, renewal and transfer rules, so have your lawyer read it and check financing with your lender before you commit.
faq.q: What does leasehold mean for a home here?

faq.a: TFN reported about 5,400 residents in September 2025, about 4,900 of them leasehold residents and about 500 in Member housing. In 2009 it was about 660. TFN projects about 10,000 by 2040 at full build-out and about 12,000 by 2050.
faq.q: How many people live on Tsawwassen Lands?

faq.a: Yes. TFN holds long-term leases for both, and Tsawwassen Mills is under a 99-year lease. Both sit in the roughly 69-hectare Mixed Use Area, where the plan allows long-term residential development tied to market demand.
faq.q: Are Tsawwassen Mills and Tsawwassen Commons on leased land?

faq.a: The Bluff in the Community Area has a heron rookery of about 400 nests, with more than 800 birds year-round. The plan also describes the Great Blue Heron Way trail. Ask TFN what public access applies before you plan a visit.
faq.q: Where can I see herons or walk a trail nearby?

faq.a: Highway 17 and Deltaport Way cross the lands. The key internal roads named in the plan are 52nd Street, Salish Sea Drive, Salish Sea Way, Tsawwassen Drive and 41B Street. TFN says it will monitor traffic on Highway 17, Deltaport Way and the 41B Street overpass.

The plan site says water, sanitary sewer and drainage services were built along with the roads, with other services supplied by third parties. Water comes from Metro Vancouver and transit from TransLink. Check your lease and strata documents for what you pay and to whom.
faq.q: Which services does TFN provide to leaseholders?

faq.a: TFN plans a Mixed Use Area Plan, an Industrial and Employment Lands Secondary Plan and a Brunswick Point Lands Growth Plan. It also lists study areas, including the 13-Acre Parcel and the Industrial Waterfront Parcel. No decisions on those are stated in the plan.
faq.q: What is planned next for the area?

faq.a: The listings read for City-side Springs buildings record apartment/condo product in the Tsawwassen Springs subdivision, and a 5011 Springs listing records concrete construction and underground parking. Do not confuse City-side Springs product with housing on Tsawwassen Lands next door, which sits under TFN jurisdiction and land law.
faq.q: Is a Tsawwassen Springs condo freehold strata or leasehold?

faq.a: More than a typical wood-frame building's, on the listings read: a 5011 Springs unit listing records caretaker, garbage, heat, hot water and sewer in the fee inclusions, consistent with the buildings' geothermal heating/cooling. The binding list for any lot is the Form B and the strata budget attached to it.
faq.q: What do Springs strata fees include?

faq.a: Listings record the later buildings as concrete — 5055 Springs ("concrete construction, geothermal heating/cooling, EV parking") and 5011 Springs ("concrete" construction in listing data). Confirm against the depreciation report, which inventories the building's components.
faq.q: Are the Springs buildings concrete or wood frame?

faq.a: Long-term, the provincial answer governs: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and no Springs-specific short-term bylaw was verified.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Springs unit?

faq.a: A 5099 Springs listing calls a unit "pet friendly"; that is marketing language. Pet number/size rules live in the registered bylaws attached to the strata document package.
None verified as built stock on the City side: zero strata and zero fee-simple townhouse complexes. The built townhouse-form homes in the wider north-side search are TFN leasehold communities.
faq.q: Are there any freehold townhouses in Tsawwassen North?

faq.a: A home under a 99-year prepaid lease structure on Tsawwassen Lands: Boardwalk's presale source states the ownership form as "Leasehold via a 99-year prepaid lease" (landowners lease to the developer, which subleases to homeowners), and Seaside's MLS reports record "Leasehold prepaid-Strata" title with strata plans EPS4960 / EPS5770. You are not buying City of Delta freehold title.
faq.q: What am I actually buying at Boardwalk or Seaside, then?

faq.a: For a City-side parcel, confirm City servicing or pull the GWELLS well record and Fraser Health's onsite-sewerage position; for a Tsawwassen Lands property, the question is TFN's.

Delta is the diking authority, maintaining over 63 km of flood protection, 31 drainage pump stations and roughly 538 km of drainage infrastructure — the system is the context, but a specific parcel's protection and drainage position is confirmed parcel by parcel, never assumed from the city-wide figures.
faq.q: What does the dike system mean for a low parcel here?

faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. None is verified by name here; a single-lot duplex sells whole. Check the title first.
faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in Tsawwassen North?
